records.label: Patient 1 (P1)

phenotypes.text: non-healing abdominal wound after surgical dehiscence
acute respiratory deterioration with presumed pulmonary edema
echogenic focus on tricuspid valve treated as infective endocarditis
pathergy with sterile pustular abscesses at sites of trauma
skin biopsy with acute inflammatory exudate, suppuration and necrosis
elevated IFNB1 and IL6 transcription in PBMCs

records.segregation: de novo; absent in parents by trio exome sequencing
quotes: The patient is a 22-mo-old male, born to non-consanguineous Caucasian parents.

Trio exome sequencing was performed on P1 and his parents; this identified a de novo variant in OTULIN, ENST00000284274.5:c.386G>C, resulting in a missense change from cysteine to serine at position 129 (p.Cys129Ser) (Fig. 1 F).

Investigations demonstrated raised inflammatory markers (C reactive protein [CRP] 100–200 mg/L) and elevated neutrophils (30–50 × 109/L), monocytes (2–10 × 109/L), eosinophilia (1–3 × 109/L), and a persistent thrombocytopaenia (below 100 × 109/L)

records.label: Patient 2 (P2)

phenotypes.text: multiple tender skin lesions of limbs
cellulitis-like plaques evolving into necrotizing fasciitis with ulceration
neutrophil and plasma cell infiltration with necrosis on biopsy

records.segregation: de novo; confirmed by parental testing
quotes: The second patient is a full-term Saudi female born to non-consanguineous parents with insignificant antenatal history. She was asymptomatic until the age of 7 mo when she presented to a tertiary hospital in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, with multiple tender skin lesions over the upper and lower limbs bilaterally, associated with a fever (38–39°C) and generalized edema (Fig. 1 E).

P2 underwent whole genome sequencing and a variant in OTULIN, ENST00000284274.5:c.385T>A, which results in the same cysteine to serine change at position 129, was identified. Follow-up testing on P2’s parents confirmed the de novo nature of the variant (Fig. 1 F).
some of her lesions progressed to a picture of tender cellulitis-like plaques evolving into necrotizing fasciitis with ulceration (Fig. 1 E).

records.segregation: p.P152L inherited from the healthy mother and also present in a healthy sister; p.R306Q occurred de novo; cDNA cloning showed the two variants were on different alleles
quotes: The patient is a 9-year-old girl who presented with persistent fever associated with leukocytosis, along with elevated serum CRP levels, sterile pustulosis and erythema nodosum, and impaired physical development.
Both base substitutions were accompanied by amino acid substitutions: c.455C>T p.P152L and c.917G>A p.R306Q (Tables 1 and S2).

Here, we report the case of a girl with neonatal-onset severe autoinflammation, neutrophilic dermatitis, respiratory distress, and growth failure (confirmed to be ORAS), who was treated successfully with the anti-TNF agent, etanercept.

notes.statement: By whole-exome sequencing of a Japanese girl with ORAS-like symptoms and her parents, Takeda et al. (2024) identified two rare heterozygous OTULIN variants on different alleles (NM_138348.6: c.455C>T, p.P152L, inherited from the mother, and c.917G>A, p.R306Q, which occurred de novo); the p.P152L variant was also present in a healthy sister and was listed in gnomAD (51 of 1,611,754 alleles) as of uncertain significance in ClinVar, whereas p.R306Q was extremely rare.
quotes: Whole-exome sequencing (WES) of samples from the patient and her parents identified two heterozygous variants of the OTULIN gene (NM_138348.6: c.455C>T and c.917G>A)
p.P152L (inherited from the mother) is a relatively rare variant in gnomAD (51 of 1,611,754 alleles, no homozygous pattern)

Her healthy sister also possessed a heterozygous p.P152L variant (Fig. 1, F and G). p.R306Q is an extremely rare variant in gnomAD (1 of 1,611,754 alleles in non-Finnish European adult population), ToMMo (not reported), Bravo (not reported), and TogoVar (not reported), and it occurred de novo.

notes.statement: Takeda et al. (2024) concluded that OTULIN-related autoinflammatory syndrome, previously known to be caused by biallelic (homozygous or compound heterozygous) OTULIN variants in an autosomal recessive fashion, can be triggered in an autosomal dominant fashion by the dominant-negative p.R306Q variant acting alone.
quotes: In the present study, we show that ORAS can be triggered in an autosomal-dominant fashion by p.R306Q, a dominant-negative OTULIN variant (Fig. 7).
Therefore, we suspect that the heterozygous OTULIN variant alone can cause ORAS in a dominant-negative fashion.

notes.statement: Takeda et al. (2024) found that recombinant OTULIN carrying the p.R306Q substitution had heavily impaired deubiquitinating activity against linear di-ubiquitin (kcat/KM 8.92 ± 1.61 x 10(3) M-1 sec-1) compared with wildtype (300.82 ± 97.49), whereas the p.P152L protein digested linear diUb as effectively as wildtype (294.79 ± 74.01).
quotes: The P152L variant protein (OTULINP152L) digested linear diUb as effectively as OTULIN WT; the enzymatic efficiency (kcat/KM) of OTULINP152L was 294.79 ± 74.01 (103 M−1 sec−1), almost the same as that of the WT (300.82 ± 97.49 [103 M−1 sec−1]) (Fig. 3 D).
By contrast, the R306Q protein (OTULINR306Q) showed heavily impaired DUB activity; the kcat/KM of OTULINR306Q was 8.92 ± 1.61 (103 M−1 sec−1) (Fig. 3 D).

notes.statement: Using structural analysis and surface plasmon resonance, Takeda et al. (2024) showed that Arg306 links the distal ubiquitin binding site and the catalytic core of OTULIN, and that catalytically inactive OTULIN carrying R306Q failed to bind linear di-ubiquitin to a similar extent as the known ORAS mutant L272P; in contrast, P152L caused only minor structural changes.
quotes: R306 seems to play a central role in linking ubiquitin binding and active center formation in OTULIN, and its amino acid substitution to Q would be incompatible with those interactions, likely impairing OTULIN DUB activity greatly (Fig. S1 A).
As predicted from the structural analysis, OTULINC129A/R306Q failed to interact with linear diUb to a similar extent as OTULINC129A/L272P

comparison of the crystal structures of human OTULIN (PDB ID 3ZNV) and an AlphaFold model of mouse OTULIN, which harbors leucine as amino acid residue 152, indicated that P152 and L152 cause only minor structural changes (Fig. 3 I and Fig. S1 B).

notes.statement: In OTULIN-knockout HeLa cells reconstituted with OTULIN constructs, Takeda et al. (2024) found that OTULIN(R306Q) was expressed at wildtype levels and bound LUBAC normally but increased TNF-induced auto-linear ubiquitination of HOIL-1L and augmented TNF+cycloheximide-induced caspase-8/caspase-3 cleavage, LDH release, and annexin-V positivity, whereas OTULIN(P152L) behaved like wildtype; neither variant overtly affected IkappaB-alpha phosphorylation and degradation.
quotes: TNF+CHX augmented cleavage of caspase-8 and caspase-3, release of lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), and Annexin-V and TO-Pro-3 positivity in OTULINR306Q-expressing cells, but not in OTULINP152L-expressing cells (Fig. 4, F–J), suggesting that the p.R306Q variant provides reduced protection from cell death.
The OTULINR306Q or OTULINP152L variants did not overtly affect phosphorylation and degradation of IκBα, which are the hallmarks of NF-κB activation, or phosphorylation of p38 and JNK
By contrast, the amounts of patient-derived OTULINP152L and OTULINR306Q were virtually the same as those of the WT (Fig. 4 A).

notes.statement: Takeda et al. (2024) differentiated patient-derived iPS cells into mesenchymal stem cells and, after base editing to replace either variant with wildtype, found that cells expressing OTULIN(R306Q) with wildtype (Edit-L152) accumulated linear ubiquitin upon TNF treatment and were as sensitive to TNF-mediated cell death as the original patient cells, and more sensitive than control or Edit-Q306 (WT/P152L) cells.
quotes: We found that the amount of total intracellular linear ubiquitin was significantly increased in MSCs expressing OTULINR306Q (patient and Edit-L152 cells) upon TNF treatment, although there was no difference in the amount of K48 or K63 chains (Fig. 6, B and C).

TNF-dependent cell death, as evaluated by cleavage of caspase-3 activation and Annexin-V staining, revealed that Edit-L152 (WT/R306Q) cells were as sensitive to TNF-mediated cell death as patient-derived MSCs and more sensitive than control or Edit-Q306 (WT/P152L) cells (Fig. 6, F–H).

notes.statement: In NF-kappa-B reporter assays and in OTULIN-null HEK293 cells, Takeda et al. (2024) showed that OTULIN(R306Q) counteracted the suppression of LUBAC-mediated NF-kappa-B activation by wildtype OTULIN in a dose-dependent manner and reversed the wildtype- or P152L-mediated reduction of linear chains and rescue from TNF-induced death, demonstrating a dominant-negative function.
quotes: Indeed, the introduction of OTULINR306Q counteracted suppression of LUBAC-mediated NF-κB activation by exogenous OTULIN WT in a dose-dependent manner, whereas OTULINL272P, a known ORAS-provoking mutant, did not (Fig. S5 B).

Introduction of the OTULINR306Q variant significantly reversed the OTULIN WT- or OTULINP152L-mediated rescue of death in OTULIN-null HEK293 cells (Fig. 7, G–I), which confirms that the dominant-negative function of the OTULIN p.R306Q variant is causative to augmented TNF-mediated cell death

notes.statement: Comparing residual enzymatic activities of OTULIN mutants, Takeda et al. (2024) found R306Q to be less active than Y244C but more active than L272P and G281R, and concluded that the severity of ORAS symptoms appears to correlate with residual OTULIN function rather than with the mode of inheritance.
quotes: We found that OTULINR306Q appeared to be less active than OTULINY244C but more active than OTULINL272P and OTULING281R (Fig. 3 B).
the severity of ORAS symptoms appears to correlate with residual OTULIN function rather than with the mode of inheritance.

notes.statement: Takeda et al. (2024) noted that ORAS, caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous OTULIN variants, is characterized by fever and autoinflammation, sterile neutrophilic dermatitis, and failure to thrive, and that anti-TNF therapy is a viable treatment.
quotes: ORAS is characterized by fever and autoinflammation, sterile neutrophilic dermatitis, and failure to thrive. Recent studies show that anti-TNF therapy is a viable treatment for ORAS (Damgaard et al., 2019; Zinngrebe et al., 2022).

notes.statement: Takeda et al. (2024) reported that their patient's inflammatory episodes responded to high-dose dexamethasone, prednisolone, or methylprednisolone pulse therapy but relapsed on tapering, and that etanercept twice weekly, begun at age 2 years, completely controlled the inflammation and allowed steroid-free remission with catch-up of physical and psychological development.
quotes: At the age of 2 years, the patient was started on etanercept (twice weekly), which completely controlled the inflammation and associated manifestations, including skin erythema.

Following etanercept-induced remission, her physical and psychological development improved. We gradually reduced the dose of prednisolone and she attained steroid-free remission with etanercept therapy.

notes.statement: Takeda et al. (2024) observed that, unlike fibroblasts from autosomal recessive ORAS patients, patient-derived MSCs showed normal TNF-mediated NF-kappa-B activation and normal amounts of LUBAC subinits in unstimulated cells, suggesting that reduced NF-kappa-B activation is not a common feature of ORAS patients, and speculated that enhanced cell death due to decreased OTULIN activity plays a crucial role in ORAS pathogenesis.
quotes: Thus, a sufficient amount of unmodified LUBAC remains in unstimulated patient-derived cells, and once stimulated with TNF enough LUBAC can be recruited to Complex I for adequate activation of NF-κB (Fig. 5 G), suggesting that reduced activation of NF-κB is not a common feature of ORAS patients.
we speculate that enhanced cell death due to decreased OTULIN activity plays a crucial role in the pathogenesis of ORAS

notes.statement: Takeda et al. (2024) noted that the p.R306Q variant is reported only once in gnomAD, in an adult aged 50-55 years, and suspected that this was a somatic variant, since a somatic heterozygous OTULIN p.R306Q variant had been identified by whole-exome sequencing in a cancer specimen; they concluded it is unlikely that a germline p.R306Q variant had been reported previously.
quotes: in only one adult categorized aged 50–55 years this heterozygous variant has been reported, although both germline and somatic variants are stored in gnomAD (Karczewski et al., 2020; Mitsuhashi et al., 2022; Sherry et al., 2001); we suspected that it might be a somatic variant because a somatic heterozygous OTULIN p.R306Q variant was identified by WES in a cancer specimen from a single patient (Giannakis et al., 2016). Therefore, it is unlikely that a germline p.R306Q variant has been reported.

notes.statement: Davidson et al. (2024) found that the OTULIN C129S variant was absent from gnomAD (v2.1.1 and v3.1.2); cysteine-129 lies in the catalytic domain and is essential for enzymatic activity.
quotes: The C129S OTULIN variant was previously unreported and absent from databases of normal variation, including gnomAD (v2.1.1 and v3.1.2).
Significantly, cysteine 129 is part of the OTULIN catalytic domain and is essential for OTULIN enzymatic activity

notes.statement: Davidson et al. (2024) showed that C129S OTULIN had protein stability similar to wildtype but failed to hydrolyze M1-linked diubiquitin. Patient fibroblasts coexpressed active wildtype and inactive C129S OTULIN in seemingly equal amounts and accumulated linear ubiquitin chains.
quotes: C129S OTULIN exhibited equivalent protein stability with similar melting temperature to wild type (WT) OTULIN in a Tycho NT.6 assay (Fig. 2 A).
C129S OTULIN, like the previously reported C129A mutation, failed to hydrolyze M1–di-Ub in a cell-free cleavage assay over a range of concentrations (Fig. S1 B).
we observed significant accumulation of M1-Ub chains in patient cells compared with HD fibroblasts (Fig. 2 E).

notes.statement: Davidson et al. (2024) found that transfecting C129S OTULIN into HEK293T cells, which express endogenous OTULIN, caused accumulation of M1-ubiquitin chains and dose-dependent NF-kappa-B activation. The loss-of-function variants Y244C and N341D did not have these effects. The authors concluded that C129S has a dominant negative effect over wildtype OTULIN.
quotes: Consistent with increased overall M1-Ub, we observed that transient transfection of C129S OTULIN, but not WT OTULIN or two representative OTULIN loss-of-function mutants, N341D (Spaan et al., 2022) and Y244C (Zhou et al., 2016), triggered NFκB activity as assessed by luciferase assay (Fig. 3 A).
Collectively, these data indicate C129S OTULIN has a dominant negative effect over WT OTULIN and may thereby drive autoinflammatory disease, even in a heterozygous context.

notes.statement: Davidson et al. (2024) found that C129S heterozygous patient fibroblasts showed reduced recruitment of LUBAC and reduced RIPK1 modification at the TNFR1 signaling complex. Their sensitivity to TNF-induced cell death, mainly apoptosis, was similar to that of biallelic ORAS fibroblasts and greater than that of OTULIN-haploinsufficient fibroblasts. TNF-induced NF-kappa-B and MAPK signaling was largely unchanged.
quotes: C129S heterozygous OTULIN and ORAS fibroblasts exhibited markedly increased sensitivity to TNF-induced cell death compared with HD and OTULIN-haploinsufficent cells (Fig. 3 G).
we observed reduced recruitment of LUBAC components SHARPIN and HOIP to the TNFR1 signaling complex in patient cells compared with HD and this was associated with reduced M1-Ub
Collectively, this data demonstrates that C129S OTULIN heterozygosity does not significantly alter MAPK or NFκB signaling in response to TNF stimulation in patient fibroblasts.

notes.statement: Davidson et al. (2024) found that catalytically inactive OTULIN bound to LUBAC more strongly in patient fibroblasts and promoted LUBAC autoubiquitination. They proposed that this autoubiquitination reduces LUBAC recruitment to the TNFR1 complex and promotes TNF-induced cell death and necrotizing tissue. In a cell-free assay, C129S did not directly protect diubiquitin from cleavage by wildtype OTULIN.
quotes: We observed a marked increased interaction of OTULIN and LUBAC in patient fibroblasts compared with HD (Fig. 5 C, repeats quantified in Fig. S1 E).
Thus, C129S OTULIN heterozygosity leads to accumulation of M1-Ub chains on LUBAC complexes, which reduces LUBAC recruitment to the TNFR1 signaling complex.

Yet, even at a 5:1 M ratio of OTULIN C129S to WT, all di-Ub was cleaved in this cell-free assay, demonstrating that C129S OTULIN does not directly protect M1-Ub chains from hydrolysis by WT OTULIN (Fig. 5 A).

notes.statement: Davidson et al. (2024) observed increased IFNB1 and IL6 transcription in PBMCs from patient 1, as well as an elevated interferon-stimulated gene score in patient fibroblasts, similar to biallelic ORAS lines. THP-1 cells stably expressing C129S OTULIN showed a similar inflammatory gene signature.
quotes: we did identify a marked increase in transcription of proinflammatory cytokines, IFNB1 and IL6, and to a lesser extent TNF in the peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) of P1 (Fig. 4 A).
Consistent with elevated IFNB1 in patient cells, we also observed an elevated ISG Score compared with HDs and OTULIN-haploinsufficent lines (Fig. 3 E).

notes.statement: Davidson et al. (2024) reported that both patients responded to corticosteroids and that TNF blockade allowed steroids to be reduced or stopped. Prophylactic antibiotics appeared to aid wound healing and reduce infections. Patient 2 remained in remission on infliximab with methotrexate. The JAK inhibitor ruxolitinib was tried in patient 1, but its benefit was unclear.
quotes: Similarly, TNF blocking therapy, Adalimumab, allowed both C129S OTULIN heterozygous patients to be weaned to low doses or off corticosteroids.
It is also notable that the addition of prophylactic antibiotics played a role in wound healing for both patients.
Otherwise, she remains in clinical and biochemical remission since starting anti-TNF therapy, and she completed her third year of life in June 2023, achieving 2 years of disease remission.

notes.statement: Davidson et al. (2024) described the first ORAS-like disease caused by a heterozygous, dominant negative OTULIN variant. In contrast, previously reported ORAS variants were biallelic loss of function.
quotes: This is the first report of ORAS-like disease caused by a heterozygous variant.
Herein, we describe the first heterozygous, dominant negative variant in OTULIN to cause ORAS, identified in two unrelated individuals.
